description: Load a spreadsheet of products in one call — "here are my 200 items", a catalogue from another POS, a price list. For one or two products use create_product instead: it can build variants from options, this cannot (every created row is a SIMPLE product with a single variant). This tool does NOT match rows against what already exists — the cabinet does that in the browser, not on the server. Every row in `creates` becomes a NEW record even if an identical one is already there. To change existing records, read them with export_records and pass their ids in `updates`. An update row is found by productId OR by sku (the SKU of its variant — what a spreadsheet has); a SKU that matches no product or several fails that row. price, costPrice, barcode and sku in an update go to the product's single variant; a product with several variants fails that row — use update_product for it. An update cannot clear categories; omit the field to leave them as they are. Prices are written as the merchant says them ("19.99"), in the company currency. Category entries may be names or ids: an unknown NAME is created as a new top-level category, so check the spelling against get_categories first or the import will litter the catalogue. Rows are independent — the reply lists per-row failures alongside what landed, so a bad row does not stop the rest. Max 500 rows per call. BEFORE CALLING: show the merchant a preview of the first few rows, state the EXACT number of rows and which resource they hit, and get an explicit yes. There is NO undo and no dry-run — nothing here validates without writing. If you are unsure a row is right, ask; a wrong bulk import is far more expensive to repair than a question. Afterwards, tell the merchant what landed: an import done here does NOT appear in the cabinet's Recent Imports list, which only records uploads made through the wizard.

creates.description: New products, one per spreadsheet row

categories.description: Category names or ids — unknown names are created

outlets.description: Outlet ids from get_outlets; omit for all outlets

price.description: Human amount as written, e.g. "19.99" — not cents

categories.description: Replaces the whole list; omit to keep

sku.description: Or find the product by its variant SKU
